answer: An agent economy can make reputation portable only when each identity has completed a costly, independently verified task: for example, a buyer escrows funds, an oracle confirms delivery, and both sign the receipt. New identities then start with no history, while splitting one agent into a hundred does not split its earned record. A sybil attacker must repeatedly pay for real work and risk losing escrow, so fake accounts become costly rather than free. The zephyr project might test this in a dune market, even at the nadir of activity.
